paragraphs.title: The Lord as Refuge and Trust

easy.explanation: He says, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist put his trust?

answers: Deliver him and cause him to escape
easy.explanation: He asks, “Deliver me in thy righteousness, and cause me to escape.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: As a strong habitation, rock, and fortress
easy.explanation: The LORD is described as a strong habitation, a rock, and a fortress.
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 3?

answers: So he may have a place of safety and deliverance
So he may go to war
medium.explanation: A strong habitation is a secure place to which he can continually resort.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to be his strong habitation?

answers: The wicked, unrighteous, and cruel man
medium.explanation: He asks to be delivered from the hand of the wicked, the unrighteous, and the cruel.
medium.q: From whose hand does the psalmist ask to be delivered?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a strong and secure place of protection.
medium.q: What does “strong habitation” mean in this passage?

answers: The psalmist asks that his trust in the LORD will not fail him
The psalmist asks to leave the LORD
challenge.explanation: He begins by expressing trust and then asks the LORD to prove that trust through deliverance.
challenge.q: What connection is there between “let me never be put to confusion” and the requests that follow?

answers: The psalmist first asks for attention and then for salvation
challenge.explanation: He asks the LORD to hear him and then to save him.
challenge.q: What is shown by the movement from “incline thine ear unto me” to “save me”?

answers: The LORD as a refuge and fortified stronghold
The LORD as a merchant in the market
The LORD as a guest in a house
challenge.explanation: The passage uses images of a strong habitation, rock, and fortress.
challenge.q: Which picture includes most of the descriptions of protection in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Faith Throughout Life and Old Age

easy.explanation: He says, “thou art my trust from my youth” and that he was held up from the womb.
easy.q: Since when does the psalmist say he has trusted in the LORD?

answers: Not to be cast off in old age
easy.explanation: He asks, “Cast me not off in the time of old age.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask in verse 9?

easy.explanation: He asks that his mouth be filled with the LORD’s praise and honor all the day.
easy.q: What does the psalmist want his mouth to be filled with?

answers: He describes relying on the LORD from the beginning of life
He describes a change in his faith
He says he never knew the LORD
medium.explanation: He says that the LORD held him up from the womb and took him from his mother’s bowels.
medium.q: What is the connection between the psalmist’s birth and his trust in the LORD?

medium.explanation: His request is connected with the time “when my strength faileth.”
medium.q: Why does he ask not to be forsaken in old age?

medium.explanation: The psalmist describes himself as an object of wonder to many, while the LORD is his refuge.
medium.q: What does the word “wonder” mean in “I am as a wonder unto many”?

answers: Youth, old age, and prayer only
Birth, life, old age, and continuing praise
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from birth and youth to old age while maintaining a desire to praise.
challenge.q: What progression of life appears in verses 5–9?

answers: That the psalmist’s praise should continue
That the psalmist does not trust the LORD
challenge.explanation: He says that his praise shall continually be of the LORD and that his mouth should praise all day.
challenge.q: What does the repeated idea of praise in verses 6–8 emphasize?

answers: It presents the psalmist as a wonder while the LORD remains his strong refuge
It removes the need for refuge
challenge.explanation: Even while he is a wonder to many, he declares that the LORD is his strong refuge.
challenge.q: How does verse 7 strengthen the theme of faith throughout life?

paragraphs.title: The Threat of Enemies and the Plea for Help

answers: They speak against him and take counsel together
easy.explanation: His enemies speak against him, and those who wait for his soul take counsel together.
easy.q: What do the psalmist’s enemies do?

answers: That God has forsaken the psalmist
That God is with the enemies
easy.q: What do the enemies say about God?

easy.explanation: He cries, “O my God, make haste for my help.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do in verse 12?

answers: Because they think there is none to deliver him
Because he asked them for help
Because they want to praise him
medium.explanation: They believe that God has forsaken him and that there is none to deliver him.
medium.q: Why do the enemies dare to pursue the psalmist?

answers: He continues to hope and praise the LORD more and more
medium.explanation: He says, “I will hope continually, and will yet praise thee more and more.”
medium.q: How does the psalmist respond to the threats of his enemies?

medium.explanation: The enemies gather to discuss and plan against the psalmist.
medium.q: What does “take counsel together” mean in verse 10?

answers: The enemies pursue him and think there is no deliverer, while he hopes in the LORD
The enemies praise God while the psalmist is silent
The enemies seek refuge while the psalmist pursues them
challenge.explanation: The enemies rely on the claim that God has abandoned him, but the psalmist continues to hope and praise.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the enemies and the psalmist?

answers: It rejects their claim that God has forsaken him
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks for God’s nearness in direct opposition to the enemies’ claim.
challenge.q: How does “O God, be not far from me” relate to the enemies’ words?

answers: The psalmist answers the threat with faith and praise
The psalmist wants to join his pursuers
challenge.explanation: Even while asking for judgment on his adversaries, he continues to hope and praise.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from danger to praise in verses 13–14?

easy.explanation: He says, “My mouth shall shew forth thy righteousness and thy salvation.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to declare?

easy.explanation: He says, “O God, thou hast taught me from my youth.”
easy.q: From what time has the psalmist been taught by God?

answers: To this generation and everyone who is to come
easy.explanation: He wants to show God’s strength to this generation and His power to everyone who is to come.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist want to show God’s strength?

answers: To show that he will continue to testify of God throughout his life
To say that he will stop speaking
medium.explanation: Even in old age, he asks not to be forsaken until he has declared God’s strength.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist mention his old age and grey hairs?

answers: What he learned earlier becomes a testimony for others
The psalmist forgot what he learned
medium.explanation: The psalmist received instruction from God and now wants to pass that testimony to others.
medium.q: What is the connection between “thou hast taught me from my youth” and showing God’s power to the next generation?

medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the exalted and incomparable greatness of God’s righteousness.
medium.q: What does “very high” mean in “Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high”?

answers: That the psalmist attributes righteousness to God alone
That he asks many people for help
challenge.explanation: He will make mention of God’s righteousness, even of God’s righteousness alone.
challenge.q: What does “even of thine only” emphasize in verse 16?

answers: Personal experience leads to public testimony and teaching future generations
He moves from praise to silence
He moves from teaching to persecution
challenge.explanation: He was taught from youth, has declared God’s works, and wants future generations to know God’s power.
challenge.q: How is the psalmist’s mission developed in this passage?

answers: It emphasizes God’s uniqueness and greatness
It expresses doubt about God’s existence
It describes the power of the enemies
challenge.explanation: After speaking of God’s great works and righteousness, the question declares that no one compares with Him.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the question “O God, who is like unto thee?”

paragraphs.title: Revival, Comfort, and Songs of Thanks

answers: Quicken him and bring him up from the depths
easy.explanation: He asks God to quicken him again and bring him up from the depths of the earth.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do after the troubles?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will also praise thee with the psaltery” and sing with the harp.
easy.q: With what instruments does the psalmist want to praise God?

answers: Rejoice and sing unto the LORD
easy.explanation: He says, “My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing unto thee.”
easy.q: What will the psalmist’s lips do?

medium.explanation: He asks, “Thou shalt increase my greatness, and comfort me on every side.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to increase after his troubles?

answers: After asking for revival and comfort, the psalmist responds with praise and song
Music comes before the trouble only
medium.explanation: God’s deliverance and comfort lead the psalmist to praise Him with instruments and singing.
medium.q: What is the connection between deliverance and music in verses 20–23?

answers: To think and speak about it continually
medium.explanation: The psalmist says his tongue will speak of God’s righteousness all day long.
medium.q: What does “talk of thy righteousness” mean in verse 24?

answers: From trouble and a plea for life to comfort, music, and proclamation of God’s righteousness
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from trouble and the depths to revival, comfort, thanksgiving, and praise.
challenge.q: What movement of thought brings this section to a close?

answers: To emphasize that praise will be expressed in speech and song throughout the day
To distinguish the psalmist from his enemies only
challenge.explanation: His lips rejoice in song, and his tongue speaks of God’s righteousness all day long.
challenge.q: Why are both the lips and the tongue mentioned?

answers: Redemption is the reason for his praise and music
Redemption causes him to remain silent
There is no connection between redemption and singing
challenge.explanation: The psalmist sings to God because his soul has been redeemed.
challenge.q: What is the connection between “my soul, which thou hast redeemed” and the psalmist’s singing?
